title: A novel method for the quantification of industrial and municipal waste materials for environmental hazard assessment
author: Arifin, Kayode, et al.

steps.title: Plan and layout RES2D ERT survey
steps.instruction: Design a RES2D geophysical survey covering the study site with six evenly spaced profiles: lines 1‑3 oriented east‑west and lines 4‑6 oriented north‑south, forming an L‑shaped arrangement that fully encloses the waste material area.

steps.title: Acquire geophysical data along six lines
steps.instruction: Conduct the RES2D electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) acquisition on each of the six profiles, recording resistivity values from 0 – 100 Ω·m for waste materials, 100 – 400 Ω·m for saturated/unsaturated strata, and 400 – 2000 Ω·m for the bedrock layer.

steps.title: Record GPS coordinates for each electrode
steps.instruction: Log the GPS position of every electrode used in the six ERT lines to enable later spatial integration of the data.

steps.title: Process ERT data to generate resistivity profiles
steps.instruction: Import the raw ERT measurements into the RES2D processing software, invert the data, and produce resistivity cross‑sections for each profile showing depth‑to‑contaminant plumes ranging between 10 m and 15 m.

steps.title: Identify lithologic layers using resistivity ranges
steps.instruction: Interpret the resistivity sections to delineate three major lithologic zones: (1) waste‑filled zone (0‑100 Ω·m), (2) consolidated/groundwater zone (100‑400 Ω·m) at depths 15 ≤ 20 m, and (3) bedrock (400‑2000 Ω·m) at depths 20 ≤ 35 m.

steps.title: Determine contaminant plume depth and extent
steps.instruction: From the interpreted sections, extract the horizontal spread of each plume and confirm the plume top lies at 10‑15 m depth; use these dimensions for volume modelling.

steps.title: Construct 3‑D rectangular prism model in Oasis Montaj
steps.instruction: Create a 3‑D model of the surveyed area in Oasis Montaj using a rectangular‑prism approach:

substeps.instruction: Define the prism length (χ) as the measured length of each ERT line.
Set the prism height equal to the plume depth (≈15 m).
Set the prism width equal to the lateral spread of the plume as observed on the resistivity maps.
Combine the six lines into an L‑shaped standard prism (purple lines in Fig. 3).
Compute the volume of the complete rectangular prism.
Subtract the volume of uncovered (black‑outlined) areas to obtain the net plume volume.

steps.title: Calculate plume volume using prism dimensions
steps.instruction: Using the dimensions from the previous step, calculate the contaminant leachate plume volume; the resulting estimate is approximately 312 000 m³ (height = 15 m).

steps.title: Collect soil and water samples from plume zones
steps.instruction: Gather representative soil and groundwater samples from locations within the identified plume extents for subsequent geochemical analysis.

steps.title: Perform pH measurement with HACH Method 8000
steps.instruction: Measure the pH of each water sample according to HACH Standard Method 8000.

steps.title: Determine COD using DR 39000 VIS photometer
steps.instruction: Analyze Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) of each water sample with a DR 39000 VIS Spectral Photometer, following the 23rd Edition Waste Water standard (2017) and ISO 17025 accreditation at the Fakulti Sains dan Teknologi, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia laboratory.

steps.title: Compile and interpret results
steps.instruction: Integrate the geophysical volume estimate (≈312 000 m³) with the chemical analysis data to assess environmental hazard risk, noting that most measured ion concentrations exceed permissible limits, while mercury in soil is below detection.
